Commentary.Commentary: With a lead of 222, Pakistan will look to bat for close to 2 sessions, or may be till Drinks after Supper. They first have to negotiate these uncomfortable 30 minutes before Tea. Stay tuned.

Not a bad batting effort from West Indies. Johnson went early but the others hung around. We can argue that starts were not converted but at least this side made Pakistan work for wickets. Bravo and Samuels had chances of scoring tons but missed. The lower middle order too, resisted a bit.

Consistent bowling from the hosts this afternoon. They ensured that they did not give any loose deliveries and conceded only 42 runs in 14.5 overs for 4 wickets. Yasir continued to torment as he ran through the tail, picking up 3 today adding to the 2 he took yesterday. Riaz and Nawaz gave him good support with 2 wickets apiece.

Not a surprising decision from Pakistan, given that they had been on the field for more than a day and bowled close to 125 overs. They had to toil hard and understandably, the bowlers need some rest. They now have 5 sessions and a bit to try and win this game.

OUT! LBW! The decision stays as it is! Yasir gets the breakthrough this afternoon. It looked very plumb to the naked eye. Dowrich walked over to Holder, had a chat and then took the review. After getting satisfied with the replays regarding no inside edge, the third umpire checked the Hawk Eye. It showed the ball to be pitching around leg and then spun on to hit the middle and off stumps. A closer look at the replays suggests that Dowrich was looking to defend but his bat got hit with the pad and hence came late. WEST INDIES NEED 55 MORE TO AVOID THE FOLLOW-ON!

PITCH REPORT - Bazid Khan doing the pitch report says that there is no deterioration because it is under cover for most of the day. The bowlers might have some assistance earlier on but once the sun sets, the pitch starts to freshen up and the ball comes on nicely to the bat.
Pakistan didn't pick many wickets in the first two sessions yesterday and would look to come back harder today. The wicket still looks good to bat on so let's see what do we have in store.

Hello everyone to the coverage of the day 4 of the first Test match between Pakistan and West Indies in Dubai. Pakistan are still on top as some late wickets towards the end yesterday kept West Indies on the back foot. The visitors are trailing by 264 runs and would be looking to add much as possible from their lower order as they have just four wickets in hand.
...Day 4, Session 1...

Wahab Riaz picked up two wickets in one spell which had some hostile short pitch bowling. Nawaz and Sohail got one each while Yasir Shah grabbed two. Pakistan were made to work hard for wickets as the wicket still looked good to bat on. They would look to bowl out Windies quickly tomorrow and bat for a bit to give their bowlers some rest. Join us tomorrow then to see how the day pans out. Until then, goodbye and take care. Cheers!

Another decent day for Pakistan! The final session keeps them on top yet again! West Indies battled hard throughout the day but lost wickets in the final session. Darren Bravo's hard-fought knock came to an end when the debutant Nawaz struck to leave West Indies reeling. The southpaw missed out on his much deserving ton as he missed the three-figure mark by just 13 runs after facing 258 balls. West Indies are still 264 runs behind and have just four wickets in hand.

Pakistan have bowled tight lines and lengths and they did taste success in the form of Samuels. The visitors still trail by 368 runs and it would be interesting to see how much will they be able to reduce the deficit to till the end of day's play. Join us in a bit for the final session.

THIS SESSION - 25 OVERS, 73 RUNS AND 1 WICKET! Another good session for West Indies! They have scored runs but have lost the veteran Marlon Samuels. Apart from that, nothing to take away from the Windies. Darren Bravo has read the wicket really well and in spite of given temptations time and time again to play the loose shots, he hasn't. PITCH REPORT - Bazid Khan says, the pitch hasn't changed much. Adds it is still a good wicket to bat on. Further says there are some footmarks and Yasir Shah will be targeting one near the leg stump of the right-hander. Informs that West Indies will have to worry about the scoreboard pressure and the trail by spin, other than that no issues.

Hello and a warm welcome for day 3 of this Day/Night Test between Pakistan and West Indies. Yesterday, it was all about Azhar Ali who was absolutely brilliant as he smashed a triple ton with some handful contributions from Aslam, Shafiq and Azam. Once the Pakistani ODI skipper got to the milestone, Pakistan said they have had enough and declared the innings with a mammoth score of 579/3.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1...

Pakistan know these conditions inside out and will back themselves to bowl better than West Indies and keep their control on the Test. Do join us tomorrow at 1700 IST for all the action from Day 3. Take care and cheers!

West Indies came out looking positive but the opening stand did not last long. Yasir Shah struck immediately to send back Leon Johnson. They still trail by 510 runs and will know they have a lot of work left. The visitors have quite a few youngsters playing for them right now and will hope that they step up. Their first target will be to avoid the follow-on, that too is still some way away.
